issues.description: Raising APIConnectionError inside _process_stream_event will be swallowed by recv_task's blanket exception handler
issues.detail: In stt_v2.py around line 246-251, _process_stream_event raises APIConnectionError for auth/quota/error message types. But recv_task wraps the call in `except Exception: logger.exception(...)` (lines 167-170), which catches the raise and continues looping. Auth failures and quota errors will only be logged, never propagated, leaving the stream silently stuck. Re-raise these explicitly or special-case APIConnectionError.

issues.description: audio_format always derived from sample_rate, ignoring unsupported rates
issues.detail: In STTv2.__init__, `audio_format = f"pcm_{sample_rate}"` is cast to STTAudioFormat without validation. Passing sample_rate=11025 or 32000 silently produces an invalid `pcm_11025` string that the server will reject at connect time with an opaque error. Validate sample_rate against the documented set (8000/16000/22050/24000/44100/48000) at construction time.

issues.description: Reconnect loop never sets _reconnect_event, so reconnection path is dead code
issues.detail: The `while True` loop in _run waits on _reconnect_event to trigger reconnection, but nothing in this class ever calls `self._reconnect_event.set()`. If the WS closes unexpectedly, recv_task raises, tasks_group completes with an exception, and `task.result()` re-raises out of _run instead of reconnecting. Either remove the reconnect scaffolding or wire a real trigger.

issues.description: send_task never sends a final commit, may drop trailing audio on stream end
issues.detail: send_task always sends `commit: False` and exits when _input_ch closes, setting `closing_ws = True` without telling the server to commit or close. Any audio buffered server-side after the last VAD-triggered commit will be discarded. Consider sending a final commit message or close frame so the trailing transcript is flushed before teardown.

issues.description: Parameter validation ranges documented but not enforced
issues.detail: Docstring states vad_silence_threshold_secs must be 0.3-3.0, vad_threshold 0.1-0.9, and duration fields 50-2000ms, but no checks are performed. Invalid values are forwarded to the API as query params, producing late, opaque server errors. Add range checks in __init__ matching the documented bounds so misuse is caught locally with a clear message.

issues.description: Default language fallback to "en" may mislabel transcripts
issues.detail: _process_stream_event sets `language=self._language or "en"` on every SpeechData. If the user did not specify language_code, downstream consumers will see "en" labels regardless of what the server actually detected. Prefer passing the server-detected language if Scribe returns it, or leave the field None/empty rather than hard-coding English.

review.summary: The STTv2 plugin adds a solid first cut at WebSocket streaming for Scribe v2, but several robustness gaps need attention. The most serious is that fatal API errors raised inside _process_stream_event are swallowed by recv_task's blanket exception handler, hiding auth/quota failures. The reconnect scaffolding is dead code (no trigger sets the event), the audio_format and VAD parameters are not validated despite documented bounds, and the send path never issues a final commit on shutdown. A minor concern: language defaults silently to "en" which can mislabel events.
